notes: The whole 43-page theme document, read end to end: the 1906 earthquake and fires, the refugee camps, the design and construction of the relief shacks, life in the camps, the Bonus Plan and Grant & Loan programmes, the closure of the camps and the removal of shacks to private lots, the 1913 Relief Survey, the preservation campaigns from 1983 onward, the survey guide, the evaluation criteria with its three worked examples, and the bibliography. It is a typology and eligibility guide rather than an inventory: it carries no appendix table, no APNs and no status codes, and the extant shacks it names are the handful that came up in landmark cases, preservation campaigns and Planning determinations. Its Table 1 lists all 31 refugee camps by name, shelter type and bounding streets — no street numbers, so no camp resolves to a parcel.

coverage.remaining: Nothing in this document. The 2016 reconnaissance survey it describes — 45 authenticated shack sites, surveyed with Jane Cryan and Curbed.com — is a separate list that is not printed here and would be the thing to go after next. Cryan's 'Hope Chest' manuscript, its principal source, is unpublished and readable only at the SF History Center.
coverage.note: 9 numbered San Francisco addresses and 2 unnumbered locations in 43 pages. Table 1's 31 refugee camps are located by bounding streets only and carry no street number.

findings.description: Two earthquake relief shacks — one Type B, one Type A — were joined in 1907 into the L-shaped house that stands here.
